t: An Igbo sacred kingdom whose priest-king, the Eze Nri, held ritual rather than military authority over much of northern Igboland.
Nri agents marked with ichi scars cleansed abominations, settled disputes and conferred Ozo titles across a wide area.
Its traditional history begins in 948; in 1911 British officials forced the Eze Nri to renounce his ritual powers.
dyk: A dignitary buried at nearby Igbo-Ukwu had been buried seated on a wooden stool; the Eze Nri, too, were buried seated, in a wood-lined chamber.
ev: Traditional date for Eri, founder of the Nri line, in Onwuejeogwu’s reconstruction
Ifikuanim, remembered as the first Eze Nri, begins his reign (traditional date)
Bronzes, beads and a seated burial are deposited at Igbo-Ukwu, near Nri
Nri influence reaches Igbo communities west of the Niger, by one reconstruction
Nri influence declines as the Atlantic slave trade and the Aro network expand
The Anglo-Aro War opens the Igbo interior to British rule
A British expedition forces the Eze Nri to renounce his ritual powers

f.founder: Eri, according to tradition; Ifikuanim, remembered as the first Eze Nri
f.successor: British colonial rule (Southern Nigeria); the Eze Nri survives as a traditional ruler
